subject: Temporary data residency override request — heap-dump triage
messages:
From: Tara Sullivan <tara.sullivan@intellimed.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform@intellimed.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Emergency: request to retain heap dump for triage (EU region)

Hi Monica,

We had a production crash yesterday (2028-01-09 22:11 CET) on our EU deployment that produced a full Java heap dump. Our team needs to keep the heap dump and associated crash logs in place for a short, timeboxed investigation window. Current retention policy is set to auto-delete ephemeral artifacts after 24 hours; that window expired overnight and we weren't able to pull the artifacts before deletion began.

Could Redwood make a temporary data residency override so the heap dump and the related crash logs are preserved for up to 72 hours in the EU region? This data contains service-level traces and a small amount of patient identifiers embedded in application-level objects — we understand the sensitivity. We only need it for triage and will redact/share only the minimal pointers when necessary.

Attachments: heapdump-20280109.tgz (1.2GB), crash-log-jan9.txt (12KB)

Please advise next steps and what approvals or controls you need from our side.

Thanks,
Tara Sullivan
Platform Lead, IntelliMed
+1 415 555 0192

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tara Sullivan <tara.sullivan@intellimed.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Emergency: request to retain heap dump for triage (EU region)

Thanks for the heads up, Tara — filing this as a short-term exception request. I want to get SRE and Security eyes on this before we take action.

Vivek / Hannah, quick summary: IntelliMed hit a prod JVM crash; they captured a heap dump in the EU cluster that would otherwise be deleted per our 24-hour ephemeral retention. They request a 72-hour preservation window in the EU to allow their debug team to triage. Attachments include the heap dump stub and a crash log sample (they flagged potential patient identifiers).

Questions I need answered before approval:
- Vivek: Can we preserve the artifacts in-region (EU) with customer KMS and break-glass auditing? Any operational risk?
- Hannah: From security/compliance perspective, what controls do we require to limit access and protect PHI during the window? DLP scan required? Redaction?

Proposed operational constraints (suggested):
- Preservation window: 48–72 hours (final window per security)
- Access: role-restricted, require break-glass ticket, all access logged and exported to audit log
- Storage: keep in customer-designated EU bucket, encrypted with customer-managed key if available
- Post-window: automatic irreversible deletion and audit record generation

Tara: we'll confirm timeline and controls ASAP.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Emergency: request to retain heap dump for triage (EU region)

Monica / Hannah — I reviewed the artifacts and the host metadata in the EU cluster. Technical notes and recommendation: 

- We can create a short-lived retention carveout for the specific artifact path and tag it to the IntelliMed tenant so only tenant-scoped tooling can see it. No cluster-level snapshot is required.
- Storage: keep the preserved copy in the EU object store namespace tied to the tenant. If IntelliMed provides a customer KMS key we can encrypt server-side with that; otherwise we will use our tenant-isolated key and perform key-rotation immediately after the window.
- Access model: break-glass via the internal incident console that creates a timebound IAM policy and records the operator identity + reason. All access will be written to the audit stream (immutable).
- Timebox: my comfort level is 72 hours maximum, but if Security wants to shorten it to 48 hours we can automate the deletion sooner.
- Risk: negligible to platform if limits are enforced and no additional services are spun up against the artifact. The main risk is accidental snapshotting — I'll disable automatic backups for that tenant path for the duration.

If we proceed, I'll implement the carveout tonight (EU timezone) and run a DLP scan job on the heap dump to identify PII/PHI blobs. That scan will not persist results outside the immutable audit.

Vivek
SRE, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 10:05 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tara Sullivan <tara.sullivan@intellimed.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Emergency: request to retain heap dump for triage (EU region)

Thanks — I ran through the requirements with Security & Privacy. Conditional approval follows with the constraints below. Once the conditions are confirmed, Monica please mark this request as approved and Vivek can proceed to implement the carveout.

Security conditions (must be met before we flip the preservation switch):
1) Limit the preservation window to 48 hours unless a renewal request is explicitly filed and approved. We prefer the shorter window for PHI-containing artifacts.
2) The heap dump must be DLP-scanned and any obvious PHI tokens redacted before any copy leaves the EU environment. If redaction cannot be performed safely we require the customer to provide a redacted subset or consent documented in writing.
3) Access only via break-glass; two-person rule for approving access (incident owner + security officer).
4) Encryption: prefer customer-managed KMS key. If customer KMS is not available, use tenant-isolated CMK and rotate key after deletion. Document key IDs in the audit record.
5) Add explicit legal acknowledgement from IntelliMed: one-line email confirming they accept the short retention exception and that they are responsible for data minimization.

Tara — if you can send a short email confirming you accept the terms above (point 5) I will sign off and we can proceed.

Hannah Schmitt
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
